region_scene_page.compact: The 1990s country boom turned Nashville stars into stadium and CD-era giants while keeping traditional country markers audible for mass audiences.
region_scene_page.standard: The 1990s country boom turned Nashville stars into stadium and CD-era giants while keeping traditional country markers audible for mass audiences. George Strait's Amarillo by Morning, Randy Travis' On the Other Hand, Garth Brooks' The Thunder Rolls, and Brooks & Dunn's Brand New Man give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: The 1990s country boom turned Nashville stars into stadium and CD-era giants while keeping traditional country markers audible for mass audiences. It can sound polished and enormous while still advertising country identity through vocal, fiddle, steel, and image. George Strait's Amarillo by Morning, Randy Travis' On the Other Hand, Garth Brooks' The Thunder Rolls, and Brooks & Dunn's Brand New Man give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
